rationale: The workflow is a reusable workflow_call that only exposes version constants as job outputs. Its single job writes environment variables to GITHUB_OUTPUT and performs no dependency installation, build, test, matrix execution, scheduling, or network fetch. None of the evidence-supported optimizations apply: dependency caching (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE, P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE) has nothing to cache; custom timeouts (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT, P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT) target runaway or slow jobs, but this job is instantaneous; fail-fast (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST) and job reordering (P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST) require a matrix; schedule suppression (P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE, P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE) requires schedule triggers; change filtering (P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER) and workflow skipping (P-LIT-SKIP-WORKFLOW) are caller-controlled for workflow_call; test/build selection and prioritization (P-LIT-PRIORITIZE, P-LIT-SELECT, P-LIT-BUILD-SELECT, P-LIT-BUILD-PRIORITY) have no tests or builds; Bazel patterns (P-LIT-BAZEL-*) have no Bazel usage; environment reuse (P-LIT-ENV-CACHE) and step skipping (P-LIT-UNAFFECTED-STEPS) have no environment setup or conditional steps. Applying any of these would be unsupported or unrelated, and could weaken the intended coverage of the version-output contract.
